summary: This RFC updates the registry of authentication method results in Authentication-Results header fields, fixing a mismatch between the original registry and the SPF specification. It was replaced by RFC 7001.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6577 corrects a mismatch between the Authentication-Results registry and the SPF specification. It marks hardfail as deprecated and uses fail for SPF and Sender-ID failures; RFC 7001 later obsoleted this memo.

questions: what does fail mean in authentication-results
is hardfail still an active spf result
which methods use the authentication-results fail value
subtitle: Aligns an Authentication-Results SPF result with the SPF specification.

tldr.problem: The Authentication-Results registry used hardfail for an SPF failure, while the SPF specification used fail.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6577 deprecates hardfail, defines fail for SPF and Sender-ID, and adds status columns to two email authentication registries.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6577 updates RFC 5451 and was obsoleted by RFC 7001.

today: RFC 6577 updates RFC 5451 and was obsoleted by RFC 7001.

sections.title: A Different Result Word in the Registry
sections.content:
RFC 5451 created registries for results used in Authentication-Results message headers. One entry used hardfail for an SPF failure, while the SPF specification used fail. RFC 6577 updates RFC 5451 to correct this discontinuity.

The defined fail result means that the client is explicitly not authorized to inject or relay mail using the sender's DNS domain.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry and the SPF specification used different words for the same failure result. This memo aligns the registry with the word used by SPF.

sections.title: Registry Status and Result Names
sections.content:
IANA added a Status column to both the Email Authentication Methods and Email Authentication Result Names registries. The allowed statuses are active and deprecated, and new registrations must specify one of them.

IANA marked hardfail deprecated and updated fail to apply to both spf and sender-id. The fail entry is active.
sections.plainLanguage: The registries now show whether each entry is active or deprecated. The fail result applies to both SPF and Sender-ID, while hardfail is deprecated.

sections.title: Security and Transition
sections.content: The RFC notes that older implementations may not recognize the corrected entry. It advises implementers to support both result strings for some period, while observing that some implementations already used the SPF-defined string. Appendix A notes that this update does not correct a separate error in an example in RFC 5451.
sections.plainLanguage: Some older software may still use hardfail, so the memo advises supporting both terms for a time. It corrects the registry entries, not every example in the earlier RFC.
